Who is it that hit you?”"}]},{"verse":69,"paragraph_start":true,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a slave girl came up to him and said,"},{"speaker":"other","text":"“You too were with Jesus the Galilean.”"}]},{"verse":70,"paragraph_start":false,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"But he denied it in front of them all, saying,"},{"speaker":"other","text":"“I do not know what you are talking about.”"}]},{"verse":71,"paragraph_start":false,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"When he went out to the gateway, another woman saw him and said to those who were there,"},{"speaker":"other","text":"“This man was with Jesus the Nazarene.”"}]},{"verse":72,"paragraph_start":false,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"And again he denied it, with an oath:"},{"speaker":"other","text":"“I do not know the man.”"}]},{"verse":73,"paragraph_start":false,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"After a little while the bystanders came up and said to Peter,"},{"speaker":"other","text":"“Surely you too are one of them, for your accent gives you away.”"}]},{"verse":74,"paragraph_start":false,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"Then he began to call down curses and to swear,"},{"speaker":"other","text":"“I do not know the man!”"},{"speaker":"narrator","text":"And at once a rooster crowed."}]},{"verse":75,"paragraph_start":false,"segments":[{"speaker":"narrator","text":"And Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken:"},{"speaker":"Jesus","text":"“Before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”"},{"speaker":"narrator","text":"And he went outside and wept bitterly."}]}],"notes":[{"verse":2,"phrase":"handed over","lemma":"παραδίδωμι","kind":"departure","traditional":"betrayed","note":"The Greek verb is the ordinary word for transferring someone into another’s custody. Matthew uses it for what Judas does, what the priests do in taking Jesus to Pilate, and what Pilate does. Most English versions say “betray” when Judas is the subject and “deliver” elsewhere, which hides that one word runs through the whole story. Many scholars regard “betray” as an inference from context and not the word’s meaning, though others defend it for Judas."},{"verse":6,"phrase":"Simon the leper","lemma":"λεπρός","kind":"background","traditional":"Simon the leper","note":"The familiar byname is kept because it identifies the man; it does not describe his present state. The Greek word covers the range of ritually defiling scaly skin conditions regulated in Leviticus 13–14, which is broader than modern leprosy (Hansen’s disease) and may not include it. Since Simon is hosting a meal, he had presumably recovered and the nickname stayed with him."},{"verse":13,"phrase":"good news","lemma":"εὐαγγέλιον","kind":"departure","traditional":"gospel","note":"“Gospel” is now a religious term or the name of a book. The Greek was an ordinary word for a public announcement of good news, and many modern translations already alternate between the two renderings."},{"verse":15,"phrase":"weighed out","lemma":"ἵστημι","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"covenanted with him for","note":"The verb can mean to place on a scale and so pay out, or to fix or agree on a sum (so the King James, “covenanted with him”). “Weighed out” is chosen because the wording echoes the Greek of Zechariah 11:12, where thirty pieces of silver are weighed out as a shepherd’s wages, a passage Matthew returns to in 27:9–10. Thirty silver shekels is also the compensation set for a gored slave in Exodus 21:32."},{"verse":25,"phrase":"You have said it","lemma":"","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"You have said so","note":"Literally “You said.” Jesus gives the same reply to the high priest in verse 64. Most scholars take it as an affirmative that leaves responsibility for the words with the questioner; some hear it as more guarded or evasive."},{"verse":28,"phrase":"of the covenant","lemma":"διαθήκη","kind":"textual","traditional":"of the new testament","note":"Many later manuscripts read “of the new covenant,” which is the source of the King James wording. The earliest witnesses lack “new,” which was probably added from Luke 22:20 and 1 Corinthians 11:25. “Blood of the covenant” echoes Exodus 24:8."},{"verse":31,"phrase":"fall away because of me","lemma":"σκανδαλίζω","kind":"departure","traditional":"be offended because of me","note":"The King James has “be offended,” which now suggests hurt feelings. The verb means to be tripped up so that one’s loyalty fails, and here it refers to the disciples’ desertion later that night; most modern versions likewise have “fall away.” The quotation that follows is from Zechariah 13:7."},{"verse":41,"phrase":"testing","lemma":"πειρασμός","kind":"departure","traditional":"temptation","note":"English “temptation” now means enticement to sin, but the Greek word chiefly means a putting to the proof, an ordeal that shows whether someone will stay faithful—here, the crisis about to break on the disciples. Most versions keep “temptation” in this verse, and a few have “the time of trial.” The lexicons recognize both senses, and the two overlap."},{"verse":45,"phrase":"Are you still sleeping and resting?","lemma":"","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"Sleep on now, and take your rest","note":"The Greek can be read as a question, as a command (so the King James), or as an exclamation, and a command could be meant ironically. A question is chosen because the next words tell the disciples to get up. The matter remains disputed."},{"verse":50,"phrase":"do what you are here for","lemma":"","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"wherefore art thou come?","note":"The Greek is elliptical, literally “for what you are here.” The King James took it as a question; most recent scholars read it as a clipped command, as here, though “Is this what you have come for?” remains possible. The word rendered “Friend” is a term for an associate that Matthew uses elsewhere in addressing someone who is in the wrong (20:13; 22:12)."},{"verse":51,"phrase":"slave","lemma":"δοῦλος","kind":"departure","traditional":"servant","note":"The Greek word ordinarily means a slave, a person owned by a master, and that is what a first-century reader would have understood. Many English versions soften it to “servant,” though some, such as the NRSV, have “slave.”"},{"verse":55,"phrase":"bandit","lemma":"λῃστής","kind":"departure","traditional":"robber","note":"The Greek word denotes an armed, violent plunderer such as a highwayman, as distinct from a thief who steals by stealth; it was also applied to insurgents. Most versions have “robber” (the King James has “thief”), and some render it “rebel” here, which is possible but not certain."},{"verse":61,"phrase":"sanctuary","lemma":"ναός","kind":"departure","traditional":"temple","note":"Greek has two words that English Bibles usually both translate “temple”: one for the whole complex with its courts (as in verse 55, where Jesus sat teaching) and this one for the building where God was held to dwell. Most English versions do not distinguish them. “Sanctuary” is an accepted rendering that keeps the difference visible, though scholars differ on how strictly the Gospel writers observe it."},{"verse":63,"phrase":"Messiah","lemma":"Χριστός","kind":"departure","traditional":"Christ","note":"The high priest is asking about a title, the anointed king Israel expected. “Messiah” conveys that to a modern reader, for whom “Christ” sounds like a name. Several modern translations make the same choice in the Gospels."},{"verse":64,"phrase":"the Power","lemma":"δύναμις","kind":"background","traditional":"power","note":"“The Power” is a reverent Jewish way of referring to God without naming him. The saying combines Psalm 110:1 (seated at God’s right hand) with Daniel 7:13 (one like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven), and the high priest hears in it a claim he judges blasphemous."},{"verse":74,"phrase":"call down curses","lemma":"καταθεματίζω","kind":"ambiguity","traditional":"to curse","note":"The verb has no object in the Greek. It is usually understood as Peter calling down curses on himself if he is lying; a minority of scholars suggest that he cursed Jesus. The rendering leaves the object unstated, as the Greek does."}],"candidates":[{"lemma":"δοῦλος","rendering":"slave","verse":51,"reason":"Recurs throughout the New Testament and versions split between “slave” and “servant,” so readers would be misled if it varied by chapter."},{"lemma":"συνέδριον","rendering":"council","verse":59,"reason":"Translators divide between “Sanhedrin” and “council” for the Jerusalem body across the Gospels and Acts, and the choice should be uniform."},{"lemma":"διαθήκη","rendering":"covenant","verse":28,"reason":"Occurs across the Gospels, Paul and Hebrews, where “covenant,” “testament” and “will” compete and linked passages need the same English."},{"lemma":"γρηγορέω","rendering":"stay awake","verse":38,"reason":"Rendered variously “watch,” “keep watch,” “stay awake” and “be alert” across the Gospels and letters; parallel Gethsemane and parable passages should match."},{"lemma":"Ναζωραῖος","rendering":"the Nazarene","verse":71,"reason":"Versions vary between “of Nazareth,” “the Nazarene” and “the Nazorean,” and the form is distinct from Mark’s Ναζαρηνός, so one policy is needed for the Gospels and Acts."}]}

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now when Jesus had finished all these sayings, he said to his disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You know that the Passover comes in two days, and the Son of Man is to be handed over to be crucified.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the chief priests and the elders of the people gathered in the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and they plotted together to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But they were saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Not during the festival, so that there is no uproar among the people.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now when Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: a woman came up to him with an alabaster jar of very costly perfumed oil, and she poured it on his head as he reclined at the table.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the disciples saw this, they were indignant and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Why this waste?

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: This could have been sold for a large sum and given to the poor.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Aware of this, Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Why are you making trouble for the woman? She has done a good deed for me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When she poured this perfumed oil on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Truly I tell you, wherever this good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told, in memory of her.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then one of the Twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “What are you willing to give me if I hand him over to you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They weighed out thirty silver coins for him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And from then on he looked for an opportunity to hand him over.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: On the first day of Unleavened Bread the disciples came to Jesus and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Go into the city to a certain man and say to him, ‘The Teacher says, “My time is near. I am keeping the Passover at your house with my disciples.”’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The disciples did as Jesus had directed them, and they prepared the Passover.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When evening came, he reclined at the table with the twelve disciples.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And as they were eating, he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, one of you will hand me over.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Greatly grieved, they began to say to him, one after another,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely it is not I, Lord?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He answered,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “The one who has dipped his hand in the bowl with me is the one who will hand me over.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The Son of Man goes as it is written about him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Judas, the one handing him over, responded,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely it is not I, Rabbi?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You have said it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While they were eating, Jesus took bread, said the blessing, broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Take, eat; this is my body.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Drink from it, all of you,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: for this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I tell you, from now on I will not drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You will all fall away because of me this night, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But after I have been raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Even if all fall away because of you, I will never fall away.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Truly I tell you, this very night, before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Peter said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Even if I must die with you, I will never deny you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And all the disciples said the same.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and he said to the disciples,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Taking along Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be grieved and distressed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death. Stay here and stay awake with me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Going a little farther, he fell on his face and prayed,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me. Yet not as I will, but as you will.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he came to the disciples and found them sleeping, and he said to Peter,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “So none of you could stay awake with me for one hour?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Stay awake and pray, so that you do not enter into testing. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Again, a second time, he went away and prayed,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, your will be done.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And coming again he found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So he left them, went away again, and prayed a third time, saying the same words again.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he came to the disciples and said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour has come near, and the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Get up, let us go. Look, the one handing me over has come near.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While he was still speaking, there came Judas, one of the Twelve, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the one handing him over had given them a sign, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “The one I kiss is the man. Seize him.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At once he went up to Jesus and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Greetings, Rabbi!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he kissed him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Friend, do what you are here for.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they came forward, laid hands on Jesus, and seized him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And suddenly one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, and struck the slave of the high priest, cutting off his ear.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Put your sword back in its place, for all who take the sword will perish by the sword.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Or do you think that I cannot call on my Father, and he would at once put at my side more than twelve legions of angels?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: How then would the Scriptures be fulfilled, which say it must happen this way?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At that hour Jesus said to the crowds,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Have you come out with swords and clubs to arrest me, as if against a bandit? Day after day I sat in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But all this has happened so that the Scriptures of the prophets would be fulfilled.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then all the disciples left him and fled.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Those who had seized Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Peter followed him at a distance, as far as the courtyard of the high priest, and going inside he sat with the attendants to see how it would end.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the chief priests and the whole council were looking for false testimony against Jesus so that they might put him to death,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: but they found none, though many false witnesses came forward. At last two came forward

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This man said, ‘I am able to tear down the sanctuary of God and to build it in three days.’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The high priest stood up and said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Have you no answer? What is it that these men are testifying against you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus stayed silent. And the high priest said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I put you under oath by the living God: tell us if you are the Messiah, the Son of God.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You have said it. But I tell you, from now on you will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then the high priest tore his clothes and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He has blasphemed! Why do we still need witnesses? Look, now you have heard the blasphemy.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: What do you think?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They answered,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He deserves death.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists, and some slapped him,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Prophesy to us, Messiah! Who is it that hit you?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a slave girl came up to him and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You too were with Jesus the Galilean.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he denied it in front of them all, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I do not know what you are talking about.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he went out to the gateway, another woman saw him and said to those who were there,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This man was with Jesus the Nazarene.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And again he denied it, with an oath:

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I do not know the man.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After a little while the bystanders came up and said to Peter,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Surely you too are one of them, for your accent gives you away.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he began to call down curses and to swear,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I do not know the man!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And at once a rooster crowed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Peter remembered the word Jesus had spoken:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he went outside and wept bitterly.

notes.note: The Greek verb is the ordinary word for transferring someone into another’s custody. Matthew uses it for what Judas does, what the priests do in taking Jesus to Pilate, and what Pilate does. Most English versions say “betray” when Judas is the subject and “deliver” elsewhere, which hides that one word runs through the whole story. Many scholars regard “betray” as an inference from context and not the word’s meaning, though others defend it for Judas.

The familiar byname is kept because it identifies the man; it does not describe his present state. The Greek word covers the range of ritually defiling scaly skin conditions regulated in Leviticus 13–14, which is broader than modern leprosy (Hansen’s disease) and may not include it. Since Simon is hosting a meal, he had presumably recovered and the nickname stayed with him.

“Gospel” is now a religious term or the name of a book. The Greek was an ordinary word for a public announcement of good news, and many modern translations already alternate between the two renderings.

The verb can mean to place on a scale and so pay out, or to fix or agree on a sum (so the King James, “covenanted with him”). “Weighed out” is chosen because the wording echoes the Greek of Zechariah 11:12, where thirty pieces of silver are weighed out as a shepherd’s wages, a passage Matthew returns to in 27:9–10. Thirty silver shekels is also the compensation set for a gored slave in Exodus 21:32.

Literally “You said.” Jesus gives the same reply to the high priest in verse 64. Most scholars take it as an affirmative that leaves responsibility for the words with the questioner; some hear it as more guarded or evasive.

Many later manuscripts read “of the new covenant,” which is the source of the King James wording. The earliest witnesses lack “new,” which was probably added from Luke 22:20 and 1 Corinthians 11:25. “Blood of the covenant” echoes Exodus 24:8.

The King James has “be offended,” which now suggests hurt feelings. The verb means to be tripped up so that one’s loyalty fails, and here it refers to the disciples’ desertion later that night; most modern versions likewise have “fall away.” The quotation that follows is from Zechariah 13:7.

English “temptation” now means enticement to sin, but the Greek word chiefly means a putting to the proof, an ordeal that shows whether someone will stay faithful—here, the crisis about to break on the disciples. Most versions keep “temptation” in this verse, and a few have “the time of trial.” The lexicons recognize both senses, and the two overlap.

notes.phrase: Are you still sleeping and resting?
notes.traditional: Sleep on now, and take your rest
notes.note: The Greek can be read as a question, as a command (so the King James), or as an exclamation, and a command could be meant ironically. A question is chosen because the next words tell the disciples to get up. The matter remains disputed.

notes.phrase: do what you are here for
notes.note: The Greek is elliptical, literally “for what you are here.” The King James took it as a question; most recent scholars read it as a clipped command, as here, though “Is this what you have come for?” remains possible. The word rendered “Friend” is a term for an associate that Matthew uses elsewhere in addressing someone who is in the wrong (20:13; 22:12).

The Greek word ordinarily means a slave, a person owned by a master, and that is what a first-century reader would have understood. Many English versions soften it to “servant,” though some, such as the NRSV, have “slave.”

The Greek word denotes an armed, violent plunderer such as a highwayman, as distinct from a thief who steals by stealth; it was also applied to insurgents. Most versions have “robber” (the King James has “thief”), and some render it “rebel” here, which is possible but not certain.

Greek has two words that English Bibles usually both translate “temple”: one for the whole complex with its courts (as in verse 55, where Jesus sat teaching) and this one for the building where God was held to dwell. Most English versions do not distinguish them. “Sanctuary” is an accepted rendering that keeps the difference visible, though scholars differ on how strictly the Gospel writers observe it.

The high priest is asking about a title, the anointed king Israel expected. “Messiah” conveys that to a modern reader, for whom “Christ” sounds like a name. Several modern translations make the same choice in the Gospels.

“The Power” is a reverent Jewish way of referring to God without naming him. The saying combines Psalm 110:1 (seated at God’s right hand) with Daniel 7:13 (one like a son of man coming with the clouds of heaven), and the high priest hears in it a claim he judges blasphemous.

The verb has no object in the Greek. It is usually understood as Peter calling down curses on himself if he is lying; a minority of scholars suggest that he cursed Jesus. The rendering leaves the object unstated, as the Greek does.

candidates.reason: Recurs throughout the New Testament and versions split between “slave” and “servant,” so readers would be misled if it varied by chapter.
Translators divide between “Sanhedrin” and “council” for the Jerusalem body across the Gospels and Acts, and the choice should be uniform.
Occurs across the Gospels, Paul and Hebrews, where “covenant,” “testament” and “will” compete and linked passages need the same English.
Rendered variously “watch,” “keep watch,” “stay awake” and “be alert” across the Gospels and letters; parallel Gethsemane and parable passages should match.
Versions vary between “of Nazareth,” “the Nazarene” and “the Nazorean,” and the form is distinct from Mark’s Ναζαρηνός, so one policy is needed for the Gospels and Acts.
